title: 3D-SubG: A 3D Stacked Hybrid Processing Near/In-Memory Accelerator for Subgraph GNNs
problem: Subgraph Graph Neural Networks have complex irregular structures with numerous independent subgraphs, creating severe bandwidth bottlenecks and poor data reuse in conventional architectures, limiting throughput.
motivation: Subgraph GNNs enhance expressiveness but their irregular structure challenges hardware acceleration; 3D integration with PIM can overcome bandwidth limitations.
method: 3D stacks logic die with DRAM die via hybrid bonding; logic die employs SRAM-based processing-in-memory macros for computation density; bit-level non-zero gathering exploits graph sparsity; workload-balanced mapping allocates subgraphs to logic-DRAM blocks; distributed global pooling reduces inter-block data movements.
key_novelty: 3D hybrid bonding integration of logic with DRAM using SRAM-based PIM macros, combined with sparsity-aware bit-level gathering and distributed pooling for subgraph GNNs.
contributions: 3D stacked hybrid logic-DRAM architecture with SRAM-based PIM for subgraph GNNs
Bit-level non-zero gathering method to exploit graph sparsity in PIM
Workload-balanced subgraph mapping across logic-DRAM blocks
Distributed global pooling to minimize inter-block data movements
146.11× performance, 934.18× area efficiency, 1171.80× energy efficiency vs. RTX 3090Ti
limitations: Comparison limited to single GPU baseline; scalability to very large graphs (>1B nodes) and multi-die deployment not discussed.
primary_theme: 3D hybrid bonding PIM accelerator for subgraph GNNs with sparsity and workload balancing
